I have been farming my land in Quzhou for over 20 years now. I am 45 years old, I only finished primary school, and I know my fields the way you know your own kitchen. My family has about 10 mu of land in total. This year, I will keep doing what works — I cannot afford to gamble with new crops or strange methods.

On 7 mu, I will grow winter wheat and then summer maize, one right after the other. The wheat is already in the ground from last October; I planted it with improved seeds I bought from the village store. Now that spring is here, I need to topdress it and irrigate. I will put down about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu when the wheat greens up — roughly one big bag of urea spread by hand across the field. I do not weigh it exactly; I go by feel, and I watch what my neighbor Aunt Wang does because she had good wheat last year. Better to put a little too much than too little — a thin wheat crop means my family goes short on flour. I will irrigate four times in total, including the winter irrigation I already did, and spray pesticides four times: herbicide once, then insecticide and fungicide when I see bugs or spots on the leaves.

After we cut the wheat in early June, there is almost no time to waste. I will plant hybrid maize seeds straight into the stubble with the no-tillage machine. Hybrid seeds cost more, but my brother-in-law planted denghai last year and his maize was heavy and full. I will apply about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu with some compound fertilizer at planting, and maybe topdress once more if the leaves turn yellow. Two irrigations should be enough if the summer rains come. Three pesticide sprays — mainly for weeds and corn borer.

On the other 3 mu, I will plant cotton in April. I will rotary-till that plot and sow improved cotton seeds. Cotton is hard work — I will need to spray about 15 times for bollworms, aphids, and weeds — but cotton prices have been decent and we need cash for school fees and medicine. I will irrigate three times. My daughter will help me pick the bolls in autumn when she is home from school.

I expect about 480 kg per mu from the wheat, about 520 kg per mu from the maize, and around 260 kg per mu of seed cotton. I am not trying anything fancy this year. Last year was okay, and I would rather follow my neighbors and sleep easy than try to save a few yuan and lose everything.
